A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Pose Prior Learner research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison despite the changed title and substantial layout reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original Human3.6m and Taichi experiments, prior and memory ablations, occlusion tests, and qualitative dog pose estimation results.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds CUB bird results, masked-reference controls, and qualitative results for additional object categories.

M1.justification: Section 3 adds a training adaptation: a randomly masked version of the input image can supply the reconstruction reference, whereas v1 requires another video frame. The hierarchical memory, affine transformations, connectivity construction, four losses, gradient handling, and iterative inference remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 retains Human3.6m, Taichi, and YouTube dogs, adds quantitative CUB-200-2011 bird evaluations, and adds qualitative 11k-Hands, Horse, and Flowers experiments. This substantially extends coverage from human and dog videos to still images, additional animal categories, hands, and non-animal objects.

E2.justification: The baseline algorithms in the retained Human3.6m and Taichi comparisons remain. CUB reuses Zhang et al. (2018), He et al. (2021), He et al. (2022b), and AutoLink from v1's Taichi comparison. The deleted AutoLink* rows were alternative scoring of AutoLink, so their removal concerns evaluation and results rather than comparator membership.

E3.justification: v2 adds masked-reference training controls on Human3.6m and Taichi. New CUB experiments use 128-by-128 images, ten keypoints for CUB-aligned and four for the other reported CUB settings, with cited cropping and split procedures. Existing training budgets, retained dataset splits, and occlusion protocols remain. Removal of the minimum-flow matching description does not establish that retained results were rescored.

E4.justification: The new masked-reference controls test whether PPL's advantage depends on cross-frame reconstruction, and Appendix A7 expands category case studies. The prior-initialization ablation, memory-size and keypoint-count analyses, and occlusion experiments are retained; v1 Figures 6–7 become v2 Figures A2–A3 without changed findings.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, statistical significance tests, or uncertainty bands. Both present point estimates and curves without uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: v2 Table 1 adds CUB results, including PPL errors of 3.19, 19.3, 18.6, 17.3, and 10.5 across its five columns. Tables 2–3 add masked-reference PPL results of 2.23 and 298.60. The minimum-flow AutoLink results of 2.61 and 302.41 disappear. Existing main PPL values of 1.92, 2.56, and 293.35 and the prior-ablation values remain. Appendix A7 adds qualitative findings for new categories.

T1.justification: The pose-prior definitions, transformations, memory retrieval and pooling formulation, and loss equations retain their mathematical content. v1's combined boundary/link-loss equation is separated into v2 Equations 5–6. Neither version contains theorem or proof developments.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion broaden the central task from learning priors from videos of animate objects to learning categorical priors from images. v1's explicit contribution of establishing evaluation metrics and benchmarks is dropped. The central claims about hierarchical memory, annotation-free learning, baseline superiority, and iterative occlusion recovery remain.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the masked-reference results as evidence that pose priors drive performance beyond cross-frame reconstruction. It adds arguments about annotation bias and hierarchical memory producing less biased priors than averaging poses, plus discussion of applicability to rigid flowers. The static-background limitation is removed, while limitations concerning 2D priors, rotations, and shape changes remain.

D1.justification: v2 documents preprocessing, resolutions, keypoint counts, and split references for the added datasets, including removing multi-horse images and aligning horses to face left. It newly states that keypoint counts match AutoLink. Existing optimizer and memory settings remain, but the minimum-flow matching disclosure is removed. Code, models, and data remain promised future releases in both versions.

R1.justification: v2 adds dataset and split citations including Wah, Choudhury, Afifi, Nilsback and Zisserman, and Zhu, plus another Siarohin 2019 paper, while removing Waissi's network-flow reference. Related-work discussion modestly refines the distinction between human-defined and learned priors; positioning relative to AutoLink, STT, HPE, and PCT largely remains.

P1.justification: The overall section sequence and much of the exposition remain. Targeted revisions change the title and author block, rewrite parts of the abstract and introduction, consolidate contributions, clarify memory terminology, and replace video-frame language with image language. Training techniques move to Appendix A6, and an Impact Statement is added.

P2.justification: v2 replaces the single-column main text with a two-column layout, adds the CUB table, and substantially reorganizes figures. v1 Figure 5 is split between v2 Figure 4 and the expanded six-category Figure A5. The memory schematic moves to Figure A4, and the occlusion plots move to Figures A2–A3. These are substantial display changes even where underlying content is retained.

improvement.justification: CUB results supply quantitative animal evidence missing from v1, while masked-reference controls address whether performance depends on cross-frame reconstruction. Additional category visualizations further support applicability. These strengthen the paper's empirical case, but the removal of the matching description and rescored AutoLink comparisons weakens evaluation transparency. The resulting net quality gain is useful but limited.
